transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-17 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (Redwood CSM), Lisa Moreno (Novaforge Head of ML), Ravi Shah (Novaforge CTO), Karen Liu (Novaforge DevOps), Miguel Torres (Novaforge SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Quarterly health check focusing on usage trends, cost drivers, recent reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment for Novaforge's LLM features.
- Novaforge currently on Hosted with increasing tail latency; exploring Dedicated / VPC for predictable throughput and data isolation.
- Action items: pricing for Dedicated, SOC2/network docs, benchmark run, sample prompts/traffic.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making time for the QBR. We'll run through usage, cost, reliability, and then roadmap alignment. Ethan, want to kick with a quick health summary?
[00:12] Ethan Park: Yeah, sure. Hi all, Ethan from CS. Overall usage up about 38% quarter-over-quarter, most of that in embeddings and the new assisted-authoring flow. Token spend up roughly 45%, and latency has been OK aside from a few spikes.
[00:28] Lisa Moreno: The embeddings are driving a lot of consumption cause we started a new semantic search index for release-candidate models. It's great but, uh, it's surprising the hourly spikes during our release windows.
[00:39] Samira Khan: Right, we've seen the same pattern in the telemetry. The tail latency spikes are correlated with parallel large-batch jobs and a couple of long-run chat sessions that don't hit prefix cache.
[00:51] Ravi Shah: On the cost side, the spike surprised our finance team — they flagged a 60% increase in monthly spend month-on-month during the release week. We're trying to understand batching configs and whether Dedicated would be cheaper.
[01:06] Jordan Lee: Totally. That's one of the reasons we wanted this QBR. We can run cost modeling for Dedicated vs Hosted with your traffic mix. Quick numbers — today you're using approx 12M tokens/month (generation + embeddings), average P95 latency 420ms but P99 hits 1.8s during spikes per our dashboards.
[01:23] Miguel Torres: I can confirm, our alerts were firing around 02:00 UTC when a nightly ingestion started. It caused a few 503s on our side. We had to manually scale some workers.
[01:33] Samira Khan: The 503s line up with auto-scaler backpressure on queued requests. For Hosted, we recommend some request routing tweaks and prefix caching for the authoring flows. For predictable throughput we can show Dedicated sizing — i.e., reserved GPU pools with burst capacity — that smooths this out.
[01:52] Karen Liu: If we consider Dedicated or VPC, how much work is the migration? Also we need to keep our KMS for key management and ensure audit logs go to our SIEM.
[02:03] Samira Khan: Migration depends on whether you need private control plane. If you choose Dedicated in our managed mode, it's fairly straightforward — pin model versions, change endpoint, keys remain in Redwood KMS but we also support customer-managed KMS with the Private option. Audit logs can be forwarded via syslog or S3 retention that you control.
[02:20] Ravi Shah: Security is non-negotiable. We need SOC2 report, ISO, and a network diagram for our auditors.
[02:26] Jordan Lee: Understood — we'll send the compliance pack and network diagram after this call. Ethan, I'll loop you in for the runbook.
[02:33] Ethan Park: Yep, I'll provide the runbook and alert thresholds.
[02:35] Lisa Moreno: On model quality, we've seen small regressions after the last quantization update. Some of the edge-case prompts return shorter completions and we've had to tweak the decoding params. Is there a way to pin a model variant without losing cost benefits?
[02:50] Samira Khan: Yes — you can pin to a specific model version or a quantized variant. We also recommend running a canary rollout and A/B evaluation with your prompt set. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles by workload to keep unit costs down while preserving output quality.
[03:06] Ravi Shah: For the benchmark, we want an apples-to-apples comparison — same prompts, same concurrency. Can Redwood run a 1M-token benchmark against the Dedicated sizing you recommend?
[03:15] Samira Khan: Absolutely. We'll provision a harness and run with your prompt set and concurrency targets. We'll also include KV/prefix cache scenarios.
[03:24] Jordan Lee: I'll send Dedicated pricing and capacity options, including an example SLO for 99th percentile latency and burst behavior.
[03:31] Miguel Torres: A question on data residency — our legal team requires EU region processing for EU customer data. Do you have region pinning?
[03:38] Samira Khan: Yes — Hosted supports region pinning for committed accounts; Dedicated and Private provide full region and VPC control. We can document the flow for EU-only routing.
[03:46] Lisa Moreno: Also, how does caching interact with our prompt personalization? We have lots of dynamic prefixes.
[03:52] Samira Khan: Prefix caching is conservative by default; it helps with repeated prefixes (like shared system prompts). For highly dynamic per-user prompts, we recommend a hybrid: cache embeddings or static system parts and leave per-user tokens uncached. We can run a simulation to estimate cache hit rate from your sample traffic.
[04:10] Ravi Shah: On procurement timing — if we decide to go Dedicated, what's the timeline? We have a product milestone at end of Q3.
[04:16] Jordan Lee: For Dedicated, typical timeline is 4–8 weeks from contract signature for a first capacity pool (depends on GPU availability). For Private (VPC) add another 2–4 weeks for network setup. We can fast-track if needed.
[04:28] Karen Liu: We also need RBAC and SSO — integration with Okta.
[04:32] Ethan Park: We support SAML/Okta and scoped API keys. We'll share the SSO integration docs.
[04:38] Lisa Moreno: Any suggestions to reduce immediate cost while we evaluate Dedicated?
[04:43] Samira Khan: A few quick levers: increase batching for non-interactive embeddings, enable prefix/KV caching where possible, pick a slightly lower precision quantized variant for embeddings, and set token limits for chat sessions. We can provide a numeric uplift estimate after we run the simulator with your sample traces.
[05:00] Jordan Lee: Ok let's capture the action items — we'll send the pricing and compliance pack, Samira will schedule the benchmark, and Lisa will provide the prompts and traffic patterns. Anything else?
[05:10] Miguel Torres: Can we get a small POC for the burst scenario — like peak hour of 5x baseline — to validate no 503s?
[05:16] Samira Khan: Yes, we'll include a burst validation run as part of the benchmark.
[05:20] Ravi Shah: Great. Also, do you have any recommended guardrails for prompt safety monitoring?
[05:25] Samira Khan: We can enable content filters and structured response validation. We'll share our best-practice doc.
[05:31] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items we discussed.
[05:36] Lisa Moreno: Thanks all. Appreciate it.
[05:38] Jordan Lee: End of call — recap in the follow-up email.

Call recap (auto):
- Usage: 12M tokens/mo, embeddings and authoring up 38% QoQ.
- Reliability: P99 spikes to ~1.8s, couple of 503s during nightly ingestion; SRE raised alerts.
- Cost drivers: embeddings and unbatched workloads; finance flagged 60% increase during release week.
- Recommended next steps: run Dedicated cost model, schedule 1M-token benchmark with burst scenario, share SOC2 and network diagram, provide sample prompts and traffic for cache simulation.

End of transcript.
